title: Validity of Conditional Adjustment When Conditioning on Treatment Descendants
banked_reason: Math referee passes, but the delivered sound calculus lacks arbitrary-DAG exhaustive recognition and a universal positive binary countermodel; the general referee grades incremental below the field floor with no bounded fix.
gap_reasons: The advertised complete constructive characterization is not delivered: core-and-collapse is proved only sufficient, and after CIDM success the algorithm returns a sound subset rather than all valid adjustment sets.

The exact polynomial procedure decides a fixed graph and specified alphabet profile by brute-force symbolic identity testing, but it does not supply the sought graphical completeness or a uniform binary counterexample theorem.
The strongest converse evidence is an exhaustive six-vertex singleton-treatment computation, so neither arbitrary graph size nor multiple treatments are covered by the semantic no-rescue result.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the core-and-collapse calculus sound, obtained an exact same-alphabet rational decision-and-witness procedure, and certified the exhaustive six-vertex irreducible null result and its at-most-six singleton no-rescue corollary. Attempts to lift these results to arbitrary DAG completeness and a uniform positive binary countermodel found no construction controlling cancellation or binary reduction; those two linked obligations remain open and prevent exhaustive MPDAG recognition.
tldr: For the fixed conditional-adjustment expression \(Q_S(p;x,y,z)=\sum_s p(y\mid x,z,s)p(s\mid z)\), core-and-collapse is a sound finite calculus even when \(Z\) contains treatment descendants. For every specified finite alphabet profile, symbolic zero testing of the cleared discrepancy polynomials, followed on a nonzero polynomial by exact finite rational-grid search, is a terminating exact decision procedure for uniform equality; every NO answer returns a strictly positive rational countermodel on those same alphabets. For singleton treatment on at most six vertices, universal validity of any \(S\) implies universal validity of the empty set. Graphical completeness, the corresponding all-vertex singleton statement, universal binary reduction, and exhaustive MPDAG success-branch acceptance remain open.
gap: The exact fixed functional is useful for estimation but is characterized in the literature only when the conditioning variables are unaffected by treatment. LaPlante, Triantafillou, and Perković (2025) assume candidate adjustment variables precede and are unaffected by treatment or outcome, and Smucler, Sapienza, and Rotnitzky (2020) require policy covariates to be treatment non-descendants; those results therefore do not subsume treatment-affected \(Z\). General MPDAG conditional identification allows such \(Z\), yet can return fractional or otherwise different functionals and does not decide whether a supplied \(S\) validates \(Q_S\).
fill: First exhaust the six-vertex singleton-treatment irreducible subclass in \(\text{oeq:six-vertex-kill-test}\). If no counterexample appears, prove the irreducible-set lemma and construct binary rational countermodels for every failed core; if a symbolic survivor appears, abandon deletion-only completeness and replace it with the smallest supported finite graphical closure described by \(\text{oeq:finite-closure-if-needed}\). Only a surviving and proved DAG converse is lifted through conditional-effect identifiability and one representative DAG.
